Table. Table 1 from rem:analytic-obstructions

Each row names a content block in which measure-theoretic language — Lebesgue, Haar, or Hausdorff — occurs, and records what the argument actually uses. Only mobius-energy-proof.md performs a genuine measure computation; every other reference invokes the language by analogy over an object that is categorical, algebraic, or given by a rational formula.

Reference What is actually used
frobenius-integration.md Calls \int_A a "categorical Haar measure" by analogy. The actual object is the Frobenius counit A \to \mathbf{1}, purely categorical — survives over any field.
categorical-laplace-transform.md Compares to Haar on \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} as motivation; the categorical Laplace transform is defined over any ground ring.
julia-set-reeb.md Mentions the Julia measure \mu_J and Hausdorff dimension d_H(q). The dimension is given by the rational formula d_H(q) = (2q-1)^2/q^3 (see birthday grading), so it lifts to \mathbf{No} exactly. The measure itself is used only for intuitive language.
statistical-mechanical-time.md, double-slit-two-modes.md Interpretive prose; no measure-theoretic computation is performed.
mobius-energy-proof.md Genuine use. The Möbius energy integral $\int_{S^1 \times S^1} d\ell(x) d\ell(y) /
